Look away at the right moments to indicate regret or remorse
Success shows as smiles, nods, and mirrored body language; smirks and nose scratches mean work harder
Breathe deeply to manage anxiety while you practice your signals

assets.visual_frame_description: A cubicle at dusk with a warm lamp; dialogue wheels sit on one side and a posture-scan silhouette on the other that shifts from OPEN to SUBMISSIVE as you choose moves.
assets.player_mission: Get your assistant to stay late on a Friday. Open with her WIIFM, sit in her visitor's chair, put your hands on her desk, lean in, hunch your shoulders, turn your palms up - then ask, stop talking, and hold eye contact. If her posture turns submissive - averted eyes, slumped shoulders, turning away - you've strong-armed her; rebuild rapport before you lose her.
key_concepts: WIIFM - 'What's in it for me?' - is the question to answer before you ask for anything
Begin with empathy; your mirror system recalls a time you felt like the other person
For an emotional request, line up with the other person's right eye; for an intellectual one, the left eye
For a woman, stand face-to-face on the outer edge of the personal zone, about three feet
For a man, stand at a 90-degree angle, three to four feet away
Persuasion signals: faster speech, varied pitch, open body posture, open palms, steady eye contact
Use smiles that involve the eye crinkle and mirror the other person's body language
After you make the request, stop talking but maintain eye contact
If you've strong-armed someone, their posture turns submissive - averted eyes, slumped shoulders
When motivation works, pupils dilate and the person nods and acts like it was their own idea
A good manager is nothing more than a benevolent manipulator

assets.visual_frame_description: A showroom floor view from behind the sales desk; two overlays - YOUR POSTURE AUDIT and HIS PRICING TELLS - with timestamps marking every deviation moment.
assets.player_mission: Audit two recorded showroom encounters. First score the buyer's posture - closed posture, crossed arms, look of indifference, closed lips, body angled away, subtle head shakes - then norm the salesperson on factual questions (list price, mpg, the color's name) and catch the exact moment he deviates from his norm while calling your price 'unlikely.'
key_concepts: As a buyer you have all the leverage, and you give it up by volunteering information about yourself
A fluent salesperson reads your age, sex, walk, clothes, and what your eyes linger on in the first thirty seconds
Retain power with closed posture: crossed arms, closed lips, body angled away, a look of indifference
Disclose neither your degree of interest nor the size of your budget for as long as possible
As the price nears your range, open up gradually - grab your opposite arm instead of crossing
Don't go from scowls to grins; the salesperson may feel played and stop playing
Ask factual questions - list price, standard mpg, the color's name - to norm his pricing behavior
If he deviates from his norm while calling your price unlikely, you're in a comfortable range
Seller tells that you have the deal: covering the mouth, fidgeting, biting the lip, darting eyes, pacing
Flushed skin, perspiring, fast shallow breathing, and nose rubbing mean he's working overtime to soften you
Politely wait him out and you'll eventually get your price or something close to it

assets.topic: Matrix: Goal x Target x Signal Set
assets.visual_frame_description: A nine-column matrix with signal chips that snap into columns; shared signals glow amber across multiple columns while exclusive ones lock in with a click.
assets.player_mission: Build the influence matrix for 9 goals - seem trustworthy, motivate, negotiate, close the deal, unite a team, seduce him, seduce her, approach a group, and make friends - and assign each of the chapter's signal sets to its goal. Mark which signals are shared across goals (open palms, eye contact) versus exclusive (right-eye alignment, thumbs in the front pocket).
key_concepts: The flirt technique: pause at the entranceway, sweep the room, then mill about before approaching
Toss your hair back to expose your neck, then brush past him with a coy 'Oh, excuse me'
Glance over your shoulder to make eye contact once more, then smile, look down, and look back up
From ten to thirty feet away, turn your back, look over your shoulder, and repeat until he notices
Men assume you are flirting if you stand too close - they can't tell friendly from flirty
To seduce her, use signals sparingly; stacking them all at once reads as predatory
Women like to be heard: make eye contact, tilt your head, nod, and show comprehension of their words
Never enter a woman's personal space uninvited
A group is open to entry with three or more people, uncrossed arms, scanning eyes, and open palms
A closed group - feet and bodies pointed at one another - means you're not invited; don't try
One person's feet poking out from the group is your entranceway; let them start the conversation
To make friends, listen twice as much as you speak

assets.visual_frame_description: A boardroom table with the client's face rendered as a live heat readout; a deal-meter swings between STALL, MAYBE, and CLOSE with every cue you correctly catch.
assets.player_mission: You've pitched the client and must now read the closing moment in real time. Watch her normed baseline for the no-gestures - folded arms, tapping, hands over the mouth, squinting eyes - that mean don't ask yet, the maybe-signals of a sip, cleaned glasses, or a chin stroke, and the yes-cluster of forward lean, open palms, pupil dilation, and eye twinkle. Fire the closing question only inside the yes window.
key_concepts: You must norm the client before you can read the critical closing moment
Whatever signals she sends after your pitch ends indicates her answer
'No' gestures: folded arms, tapping, hands over the mouth, eye squinting - don't end your pitch yet
Once she verbally says no, it's tough to turn it around, so try a different tack first
'Maybe' signals: taking a sip of a drink, cleaning her glasses, or stroking her chin
Keep additional convincing points ready to capitalize on her indecision
'Yes' cluster: a change in overall body language, smile, enhanced eye contact, and nodding
Forward lean, direct body orientation, open palms, and straightened posture all say yes
Pupil dilation, blushing, shallow breathing, and an eye twinkle confirm the sale
Look for deviations from the norm - the transitions as people make up their minds
Detect whether she's thinking 'No way do I want this' or 'Yes, but I want a better price'

chapters.title: Chapter 9: Become a Master Communicator: The Reiman Rapport Method

assets.visual_frame_description: A ten-step ladder runs down the left edge of the screen; each correctly tagged clip lights a glowing rung, and violation clips shake the ladder red.
assets.player_mission: Screen 15 clips of the same interaction and identify which of the ten Reiman Rapport Method steps each clip demonstrates - relaxed face, body symmetry, social smile, handshake, nod-mirror-lead, contained gestures, pitch variation, space respect, anchoring, or plan of action. Also flag the violations: clenched teeth, a snooty chin angle, gum-exposing smiles, gestures above the chin, and bubble-penetrating reaches.
key_concepts: The Reiman Rapport Method is a ten-point system for congruent, welcoming body language in any situation
Master each step for at least one week - ideally three - before adding the next
Practice several times a day, at least three to five, to make the changes permanent habits
A smooth forehead is one of the main ways your face tells others you are relaxed
The relaxation mantra: 'Scalp, forehead, eyelids, cheeks, mouth, jaw'
People avoid insecure people because mirror systems make their anxiety contagious
The content of spoken words makes up less than 10 percent of the impact of your message
Any two humans using these ten key signals are brought closer and kept 'in sync,' often for life
Before a meeting, take a slow deep breath, release it fully, and relax your scalp down through your jaw
Make sure your teeth aren't clenched and your chin and jaw are relaxed

assets.visual_frame_description: A split screen: the imagined interview plays on a mental projection screen at left while the physical rehearsal room at right lets you pick each move of the sequence.
assets.player_mission: Walk the group interview exactly as the Plan of Action prescribes: research names, pronunciations, and backgrounds first, script responses to anticipated questions, then role-play the entry - smile at the door, arms and legs in sync, weight equal on both legs, meet her eyes, say your name as you shake - and finish by buttoning your suit jacket and repeating each person's name at the good-byes.
key_concepts: A POA is a step-by-step recipe for a positive experience you want to happen in the future
Research first: scope the entrance, call the switchboard for name pronunciations, Google each person's background
Recite the full POA sequence out loud to yourself, picturing the events clearly in your mind
Repeat the sequence four or five times a day during the week leading up to the event
Repeated visualization tricks your brain into believing the event has already happened
Nod two to three times at least every 30 to 45 seconds while the other person is talking
Make it a personal rule to never interrupt - interruption says 'My thoughts are more important'
Mirror with similar but not identical movements; picking up a fork mirrors a glass of water
Mirror speech speed - a slow talker is thrown by a fast talker, and vice versa
To test rapport, lead: make a different movement, like unfolding your arms; if they follow, you're in
Even after hundreds of engagements, Reiman arrives an hour early and shouts 'Hello, everybody!' to own the room

assets.visual_frame_description: A video desk with freeze-frame audit rings: a green ring clicks around each correct handshake element while a posture grid overlays the standing frame and a gesture-box wireframe tracks the hands.
assets.player_mission: Audit a recorded handshake and two minutes of posture, gesture, and speech. Check the handshake rules - step in, lean slightly forward, right eye aligned, full palm, thumb straight up, elbow slightly bent, two to three seconds - then audit body symmetry (weight balanced, spine like a stack of dice, chin parallel to the floor, feet pointed at the person) and gesture discipline inside the hipline-to-chin box.
key_concepts: Approach, lean slightly forward, look him in the eye, extend your right hand horizontally, and introduce yourself
Always shake with the right hand, never the left - shift any carried items to your left hand
Grip like holding hands: easy, comfortable pressure that suggests self-confidence and enthusiasm
Align your right eye with his right eye; a thumb pointing straight up ensures a neutral handshake
A slightly bent elbow means the right distance; shake the entire arm, not just the wrist or fingers
Finish by opening your hand wide; the whole handshake should last no more than two to three seconds
Extend your hand first to be unconsciously seen as the person in control - confident, warm, welcoming
Balance your weight equally on both feet with arms at your sides; see the spine as a stack of dice
Elongate the neck, drop the shoulders, draw in the belly button, keep the chin parallel to the floor
Crossing your arms or legs throws off the symmetry and makes you appear closed off
Feet pointed at the person signal powerful interest and make the other person feel heard and valued

assets.topic: Matrix: Method Step x Situation x Function
assets.visual_frame_description: A 10x6 matrix with step tiles that expand into function notes - 'ANCHOR: cements pride at the trophy moment' - while the two advanced-mirroring tiles glow purple with a MASTER-ONLY seal.
assets.player_mission: Build the master matrix: all 10 method steps against 6 situations - job interview, sales close, party entry, a parenting crisis, a bully boss, and a first date - and map what each step contributes in each context. Flag the advanced mirroring pair (breathing and blink matching) as expert-only, with blink matching marked as high-risk.
key_concepts: Mirror breathing: diagnose a chest breather versus a belly breather, then match the style to sync up
Rapid breathing at the start of an encounter may be nerves - don't mirror that or he'll never calm down
Mirror blinking: gauge his rate over the first minutes, then match it; he'll read it as his own state
Blink matching is very difficult and can easily backfire - only attempt it as a true Master Communicator
The personal bubble extends two to three feet away from your body
Personal zones are larger in North America and Northern Europe than in countries farther south
A 'mush' - a touchy-feely person - won't mind an arm touch; the people who mind will really mind
Wait for the other person's signal - a touch on the arm, an approach - before entering the bubble
Touch the forearm with pointer and middle finger to make a key point stick; withdraw within two or three seconds
In a crisis with a child, drop the parent stance: crossed arms, leaning on one leg, the skeptical eyebrow
Get down to your child's level, look them in the eye, and label the feeling - 'It looks like you're upset'
Never say 'Stop crying' or 'That didn't hurt' - that's how we make kids into nonverbal idiots

assets.topic: Boss Battle: The Master Communicator Certification
assets.visual_frame_description: A rehearsal stage with an examiner's panel; a ten-step progress rail fills as you execute each element while a violation buzzer flashes red at every miss.
assets.player_mission: Run a full simulated first meeting as a timed certification exam: relax your face at the door, hold symmetric posture, flash your crafted social smile, deliver the perfect handshake, keep the nod-and-mirror rhythm, punctuate with contained gestures, vary your pitch, respect the bubble, then anchor her moment of joy with a well-timed forearm touch - and if she follows your lead, you pass. Violations - gestures above the chin, lingering touch, gum-showing smiles - cost points.
key_concepts: Craft the social smile in the mirror like a resume: crinkle in the crow's-feet, slight cheek lift, no gums
Smile with your eyes - they close slightly when you get it right - and diminish any nostril flaring
People unconsciously return a smile, touching off a biochemical cascade of pleasurable feelings
Keep hands open with palms exposed, inside an imaginary box from hipline to chin, shoulder to shoulder
Gestures above the chin read as erratic and flamboyant; overgesticulators seem silly and scatterbrained
Contained gestures that match your speech convey energy, original ideas, and fluent thinking
The palm-down gesture says 'I'm the expert on this part'; flipping palms over hands the discussion to them
Low pitch is universally preferred; high pitch signals anxiety because stress contracts the vocal cords
The voice originates in the diaphragm: belly button expands on the inhale, contracts on the exhale
An anchor links a strong emotion to a gesture, word, or sound - like the shower music in Psycho
Touch the forearm or speak louder at the peak of her recollection - 'Wow, that's amazing!'
Anchor pride with a hug, thumbs-up, or forehead kiss when your child wins a trophy
